title: Round-trip into string APIs
blurb: Feeds a CSSPseudoElement's selectorText vs legacy type key into getComputedStyle(), Element.animate({ pseudoElement }), and Element.pseudo(), including inside a live view transition.
question: Where does the pre-160 pseudo.type workaround break when passing a CSSPseudoElement into getComputedStyle(), Element.animate(), and Element.pseudo()?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless: pseudo.type works for ::before, ::after, and ::marker, but for ::view-transition-group(panel) during a live transition getComputedStyle returns empty values, Element.animate throws SyntaxError ('::view-transition-group is a syntactically invalid pseudo-element'), and pseudo(type) returns null. Native selectorText execution requires Chrome 160+.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (including live startViewTransition); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Passing CSSPseudoElement.type to Element.animate({ pseudoElement }) throws SyntaxError for parameterized pseudo-elements like ::view-transition-group
friction.repro: Inside a live view transition, call document.documentElement.animate(keyframes, { pseudoElement: pseudo.type }) where pseudo is html.pseudo('::view-transition-group(panel)'); Chromium throws SyntaxError and getComputedStyle returns an empty declaration.
friction.workaround: Use pseudo.selectorText when available; on older browsers that lack selectorText, track the full parameterized selector string alongside the CSSPseudoElement reference.
